canonical_statement: The study asks how strongly temporal misgrounding limits state-of-the-art LLM and RAG accuracy when the date-applicable legal answer differs from current law.
The authors define temporal misgrounding as substituting the currently in-force version of a legal article for the version applicable to the question’s temporal context.

The paper attributes static legal-RAG failure to stable article identifiers across versions, date-dependent correctness, high cross-version semantic similarity, and retrieval systems that lack temporal conditioning.

The versioned legislation corpus was built from the official PISTE Légifrance API by enumerating stable article identifiers and retrieving each article’s complete version history with validity dates, status, and full text.
The final tax-legislation corpus contains 32,436 article-versions across six tax codes.
The CGI principal corpus contains 21,040 versions across 3,696 distinct articles.
The CGI principal corpus averages 5.69 historical versions per article.
Across all six tax codes, the corpus averages 4.02 versions per stable article identifier.
The versioned corpus spans 93 years, from 1938 through future-effective provisions extending to 2031.
Article 81 has 94 distinct historical versions, the deepest version history reported in the corpus.

The auxiliary jurisprudence-linking pipeline extracts French tax citations with regular expressions, applies proximity and fiscal-context filters, resolves article identity, and selects the version valid at the decision date.
The jurisprudence-linking dataset contains 69,208 version-aware links across 32,034 distinct decisions.
Ninety-seven percent of jurisprudence links point to a version whose validity period strictly includes the decision date.
A stratified audit of 100 jurisprudence links found 98–99% link-level precision.
Against a manually annotated 50-decision gold standard, the linker achieved 88.6% article-level precision, 53.4% article-level recall, and 97% decision-level recall.
On the same 50-decision gold standard, article-level recall was 53.4%.
On the same 50-decision gold standard, decision-level recall was 97% (33 of 34 decisions containing at least one nominative CGI/LPF citation received a correct link).

population.label: Gold-standard decisions with at least one nominative CGI/LPF citation

canonical_statement: Cross-validation against parseable Judilibre visa fields produced 37.6% article-level recall after fuzzy stem matching.

population.label: Judilibre decisions with parseable CGI/LPF visa

canonical_statement: Jurisprudence-link recall is uneven and misses citations deep in long decisions and LPF procedural articles; the authors propose a fine-tuned legal NER extractor as the next step.

The scored R3 temporal-reasoning benchmark contains 209 expert-reviewed, all-model-hard questions across 33 CGI articles; 221 curated questions are released and 12 are excluded from scoring as out of scope or flawed.
The scored R3 set spans seven fiscal sub-domains and 36 years of statutory drift from 1989 through 2025.
R3 answers are scored deterministically using atomic nuggets: article identifiers by regex and numeric values by numeric-with-tolerance matching after arithmetic normalization; no LLM judge is used.
The paper reports four benchmark regimes: R1 citation extraction, R2 deterministic computation, R3 temporal reasoning, and R4 multi-document synthesis; the controlled experiment centers on R3.
The article-identifier nugget is already present in the question text for 175 of 209 scored R3 questions (83.7%), so value retrieval dominates the discriminative signal.

concept.text: Questions whose article nugget fires from the prompt

canonical_statement: The all-model-hard selection filter drops any candidate whose date-applicable gold value is produced by any evaluated model in any of four closed-book sampling draws.
The current-version divergence filter leaves 208 of 209 scored questions whose gold date-anchored value is absent from the currently in-force article text.

concept.text: Questions with gold value absent from current text

canonical_statement: The 209-question scored set was frozen before retriever or reranker development, and all 221 curated questions were cross-checked against the corpus with manually annotated nuggets and canonical answers.
A qualified French tax professional reviewed the curated questions for correctness; the auxiliary jurisprudence links were not used as R3 ground truth.
Condition A evaluates LLM-only parametric knowledge with no retrieval or web access.
Condition B is a charitable static-RAG baseline: it is given the gold article identifier but serves only the current in-force version.
Condition C_or is an oracle-article ablation that serves the date-applicable version of the gold article, isolating version selection once article retrieval is solved.

Condition C_prod is an end-to-end version-aware retriever that fuses a domain-adapted dense channel with BM25 using reciprocal-rank fusion, selects the top five unique articles, and resolves each to the date-applicable version before prompting the LLM.
The experiment evaluates eleven answer models: six closed/frontier entries including the Gemini substitute and five open-weight systems.

All retrieval conditions use the same labeled-article prompt and an 8,000-character-per-article query-windowed budget, with a pre-scoring check that the gold value is present in the served window for all 209 scored questions.
Cluster-aware inference treats model as the unit of inference and resamples articles rather than questions in 10,000 bootstrap iterations with seed 42.
Condition A (LLM-only) achieved 3.0% pooled mean strict accuracy, with a cluster-bootstrap 95% CI of 1.4% to 4.7%.

population.label: FiscalQA Pro R3 scored questions answered by eleven evaluated models

canonical_statement: Condition B (static current-version RAG) achieved 2.7% pooled mean strict accuracy, with a cluster-bootstrap 95% CI of 1.3% to 4.8%.

Leave-one-article-out pooled C_prod strict accuracy ranged from 98.1% to 99.2%, indicating that no single article carried the aggregate result.

canonical_statement: Uniform full-text prompting reduced C_or performance on long articles through long-context distraction, motivating the query-windowed extraction policy.
Because Condition B always retrieves the current version, all B-condition errors on the scored drifted set are classified as current-law substitution.
In the article 219 case study, LLM-only and static RAG answer 25%, while version-aware retrieval returns the applicable 2018 version and the correct 33⅓% corporate income tax rate.

concept.text: Standard corporate income tax rate for fiscal years opening on or after 1 January 2018

canonical_statement: The authors release the versioned corpus, jurisprudence links, benchmark questions and nuggets, audit and gold-standard samples, model responses behind Table 1, deterministic scorer, experiment harness, statistics code, and supporting documentation.

The end-to-end C_prod retriever is not released: its domain-adapted encoder weights, multi-version index, and inference code are proprietary, although per-question responses allow independent re-scoring.

The dense encoder fine-tuning overlaps the benchmark at the article level for 28 scored questions across four scored articles, but none of those questions’ historical gold values appear in any training passage.

population.label: Scored R3 questions with article-level encoder-training overlap

concept.text: Questions with historical gold values appearing in training passages

canonical_statement: The controlled benchmark is restricted to French tax law and does not directly establish performance in other jurisdictions or legal domains.
The scored R3 set contains 209 questions across 33 articles and is intentionally smaller than broad legal benchmarks because it prioritizes expert-reviewed, all-model-hard temporal-drift cases.
The single-anchor R3 experiment evaluates only current-law substitution; future-law leakage, wrong-amendment resolution, and multi-version comparison remain unevaluated failure modes.

The authors conclude that legal QA over mutable statutes should be treated as a temporally indexed retrieval problem and that explicit version indexing plus date-conditioned retrieval largely closes the measured temporal-misgrounding gap.
The paper states that legal-AI outputs should be verified by a qualified professional and should not be treated as legal advice.
